title: Wirecard collapse after €1.9 billion missing
trigger: Wirecard disclosed that €1.9 billion in cash held by a third-party trustee in the Philippines likely did not exist, leading to insolvency proceedings and the arrest of CEO Markus Braun.

timeline.event: Financial Times publishes first article questioning Wirecard's accounting practices
Wirecard admits €1.9 billion in trust accounts likely does not exist
Wirecard files for insolvency; CEO Markus Braun is arrested
Jan Marsalek, former COO, goes missing

outcome.summary: Wirecard collapsed in June 2020 after admitting €1.9 billion likely did not exist. CEO Markus Braun was arrested. Former COO Jan Marsalek disappeared and remains at large. The company filed for insolvency. The collapse led to reforms in German financial regulation and the resignation of BaFin officials.

claims.text: The Financial Times began publishing articles in January 2019 questioning Wirecard's accounting and business practices
On June 18, 2020, Wirecard disclosed that €1.9 billion held by a third-party trustee in the Philippines likely did not exist
Wirecard filed for insolvency on June 25, 2020 and CEO Markus Braun was arrested the same day
Former COO Jan Marsalek disappeared on June 29, 2020 and remains at large
